description:
A group of young people united for the sake of scientific development and the democratization of astronomy for children.

Our goal is simple: a solution to a complex problem.

Bringing the future into our own hands is not just about evolving our way of thinking; it is also about making knowledge accessible to the public.

An idea held by a single individual is just one idea; within a group, it becomes a seed that germinates into a future of peace.
summary: Is an educational space exploration game that allows players to design and simulate a mission to Europa, one of Jupiter’s moons, which is believed to contain a vast ocean beneath its icy surface. Players make engineering decisions by selecting rockets, trajectories, energy systems, scientific instruments, and crew while managing limited budgets and resources. They then pilot a submarine through different ocean zones, facing randomized challenges and discovering real scientific data from NASA missions, including Europa Clipper and Galileo. The project addresses the challenge of making space exploration and planetary science more accessible and engaging through interactive gameplay. By transforming complex scientific and engineering concepts into hands-on experiences, Abismo de Europa helps players understand the trade-offs and difficulties involved in exploring distant worlds. It aims to inspire curiosity about space, encourage scientific learning, and make NASA research accessible to students and space enthusiasts through a game that runs on computers and mobile devices
